title: GST Notices Uploaded to the Wrong GST Portal Section Deny a Fair Hearing: Bombay High Court Sets Aside Rs 62.42 Lakh Demand
case_name: Abracadabra India v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.
card_summary: A Division Bench set aside a Rs 62,42,948 GST demand against Abracadabra India, finding the notice sat in the portal's 'Additional Notices and Orders' section rather than the 'View Notices and Orders' tab taxpayers actually check. The company learned of the case only from a phone call from officials in November 2023, after the 31 March 2023 order was passed. The court treated this as a denial of a fair hearing.
card_tip: If a GST demand was confirmed without any reply from the taxpayer, check which portal tab carried the notice; one buried outside the regular tab can get the order set aside for denial of hearing.
verification_notes: LiveLawBiz, Taxscan and Taxguru all report the 16 October 2026 date, the bench, the Rs 62,42,948 figure, the 31 March 2023 order under challenge, and the finding that notices sat in the portal's additional/alternate section rather than the regular notices tab. Sources differ on whether the court quashed the order outright or remitted it for fresh proceedings with limitation kept open; card describes the common ground (the demand was set aside for denial of hearing) without asserting the disputed remedy detail.
